headline: Housing Surges, Chips Slide as Market Splits at Midday
body_html:
Stocks are showing a split screen at midday Thursday, with 301 of the 544 names we track higher and 238 lower. Prices are still moving and nothing here is final, but the dispersion is already plain: housing and software lead, while chips and energy carry the heaviest losses.

Homebuilders top the sector table with a gain of 4.94%, and Lennar is up 7.77%. Software has added 1.82%, consumer names 1.80% and healthcare 1.18%. On the other side, semiconductors are down 5.80% and energy 3.45%, while industrials and materials are each off roughly 1.4% to 1.5%. Chip-linked names fill much of the loser list: Vicor is down 14.12%, Ichor 13.60% and MaxLinear 13.19%.

The standout mover is Forgent Power Solutions, down 23.9%, followed by Carpenter Technology, which has lost 20.7%. On the upside, Badger Meter has jumped 11.46%. Into the close, watch whether the homebuilder rally holds, whether the semiconductor selling deepens, and how Gulf security headlines play in the background. Friday's session follows.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Set the Pace
briefs.body: Homebuilders are the strongest group in our universe midday, up 4.94%. Lennar is among the biggest individual gainers at 7.77%. With the sector far ahead of every other group, the close will show whether buyers stay committed.

briefs.headline: Chip Names Take the Brunt
briefs.body: Semiconductors are the weakest sector at midday, down 5.80%. Vicor has dropped 14.12%, Ichor Holdings 13.60% and MaxLinear 13.19%. The selling reaches equipment and power-module suppliers as well as chip designers, so it is not confined to one corner.

briefs.headline: Industrial Casualties Deepen the Damage
briefs.body: Forgent Power Solutions is the session's steepest faller so far, down 23.9%. Carpenter Technology has shed 20.7% and Graco 13.89%. Those losses help explain why industrials as a group are lower by 1.41% even as Badger Meter and Allegion post double-digit and near-double-digit gains.

briefs.headline: Gulf Tensions Cloud the Energy Picture
briefs.body: Reports say Houthi strikes hit Saudi Arabia, Gulf markets fell, and Saudi Aramco told staff to leave its Dhahran headquarters, according to sources. Energy shares in our universe are down 3.45% at midday. The regional risk is the headline to track into the afternoon.

briefs.headline: Consumer Earnings Land Well
briefs.body: Procter & Gamble reported better-than-expected results, with sales up 4% on laundry and home products. Comcast also topped forecasts as media revenue made up for a softer connectivity business. Consumer names are up 1.80% midday, and Vital Farms has jumped 11.02%.

briefs.headline: Layoffs Stay Scarce
briefs.body: Weekly jobless claims are near their lowest level since the 1960s, extending a pattern of few layoffs. A steady labor market supports consumer spending. That backdrop sits alongside a survey showing Americans' approval of the president's handling of the economy at a record low.
